questions.explanation: PW of A's debt to B = (1573 × 100) / 121 = 1300. PW of B's debt to A = (1444.50 × 100) / 107 = 1350. B owes more PW, so B should pay A ₹ 50.

key_explanation_from_book.present_worth: Present Worth (P.W.) is the amount which, if put at the given rate of simple interest for the given time, becomes the sum due.
key_explanation_from_book.true_discount: True Discount (T.D.) = Sum Due − Present Worth.
key_explanation_from_book.present_worth_formula: P.W. = Sum Due × 100 / (100 + R × T), where R is the annual rate percent and T is time in years.
key_explanation_from_book.true_discount_formula: T.D. = Sum Due × R × T / (100 + R × T).
